$comment: TF-C96 D-CSUBSET-ZERO-LENGTH-ARRAY-MEMBER: the GNU zero-length trailing array member (`unsigned long long tail[0];`) contributes ZERO bytes — the pre-C99 flexible-array idiom the macOS SDK still ships at `sys/mount.h:366` (`uint64_t ns_threadids[0];` in `struct netfs_status`), the 1 residual of sqlite os_unix.c that DSS rejected as `error[S000C] got [0]`. ISO C forbids `[0]` (6.7.6.2p1), so the rejection was honest fail-loud; native clang accepts it silently, so the goal leg cannot go green without admitting it. The observable property is SIZE + LAYOUT, so that is what is measured: three with-`[0]` structs each against a TWIN that is the same declaration with the member DELETED — NsWide{u64;u64[0]} vs {u64} = 8==8, NsSplit{u32;u32;u64[0]} vs {u32;u32} = 8==8 (the deliberate one: the u64[0] raises ALIGNMENT to 8 while contributing no bytes, and the two leading u32s already fill 8, so a correct impl still lands on 8 and one that charges 8 bytes lands on 16), NsByte{u32;char[0]} vs {u32} = 4==4 (the no-alignment-bump case). All six sizes and all three tail offsets MEASURED natively with Apple clang on arm64 Darwin. The exit is built from those facts, never from a `? 42 : 0` verdict: sizeof 8+8+4 = 20, plus the tail offset in each from POINTER ARITHMETIC on a REAL object (8+8+4 = 20), plus a value written to a sized member at runtime and read back (2) = 42. The sizeof terms fold, but they fold THROUGH the layout engine — there is no path to 42 that does not go through a zero-sized member. RED-ON-DISABLE: revert the admission -> `error[S000C]` array length out of range at the declaration -> no binary (MEASURED analogue: `[0]`->`[1]` exits 1, the twin-equality guard). Target- and format-agnostic (all 4 legs); clang -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra cross-checked clean at -O0 and -O2, same source exits 42.
